# forecast-geography-v2

189 runs, 63 configurations, seeds 42, 43, 44. Ranking `ranking-e53fd92c4f32`: US weight 0.2, admissions 1.0, ED 0.5. Lower WIS ratio is better; 1 = hub ensemble. Figures, table and appendix are regenerated by `planner rank`; `C<k>` labels are ranking positions, see the appendix.

## Write-up

<!-- write-up: kept across regenerations -->

**No-mask follow-up completed:** removing masking worsened 29/32 selected
formulations; the original mixed-summary leader worsened 1.036 → 1.121.
The [same main report](conclusions.md#follow-up-removing-artificial-masking-mostly-hurt)
now includes matched comparisons and inline paired fan plots.


## Fan plots: the three leading models

Shown directly below: the Hub ensemble, mixed covariate summaries, smoothed new
flu covariates, and Kinsa summaries. The models were selected by three-seed mean
WIS; all fans use **seed 42**, not the best seed. Black curves are final truth;
fans show medians and 50%/90% intervals at four-week reference intervals.
The native US and North Carolina are shown; these are illustrative locations,
not substitutes for all-location scores. Hub fans appear only where benchmark
support exists.

### US admissions

![US admissions: Hub ensemble and three leading models](best-fans/fans-US-hosp.png)

### US ED proportions

![US ED proportions: Hub ensemble and three leading models](best-fans/fans-US-ed.png)

### North Carolina admissions

![North Carolina admissions: Hub ensemble and three leading models](best-fans/fans-NC-hosp.png)

### North Carolina ED proportions

![North Carolina ED proportions: Hub ensemble and three leading models](best-fans/fans-NC-ed.png)

The [B0 comparison](b0-comparison.md) explains the target-availability and training-protocol differences.


See the [matched analysis and conclusions](conclusions.md). All 189 runs completed.
Mixed covariate summaries improve paired WIS by 7.6% versus the independent
no-covariate control (3/3 seeds), but remain worse than the Hub ensemble overall.
Smoothed new flu covariates and Kinsa summaries are promising. Geographic
attention generally worsens the corresponding independent models.

<!-- end write-up -->
